rule_changes.found: BrightFunded replaced its plans on 16 Nov 2026. The 1-Step is now 'BrightFunded 1-Step (OLD)', for accounts bought before that date; its help article (14284743, renamed) says: 'Your rules do not change, except for inactivity: it is now a hard breach and reactivation can be requested until 30 Nov 2026 only.' brightfunded.com/1-step now opens 1-Step Daily: on $100K, €497, a 10% target, and by the help centre the same 3% daily loss and 6% max loss trailing equity in real time; but no minimum trading days, payouts any day from the first funded trading day with 1% of the account kept as a buffer, and a split of 80% (90% with a paid add-on). The help centre's per-plan table, reward split and consistency articles are marked OLD as well. troid's compare and the rules above show 1-Step Daily from 2026-11-17.

2-Step Classic is now an OLD plan only, for accounts bought before 16 Nov 2026 (help centre article 14284844, renamed); neither the product page nor the comparison table lists it. 2-Step Bright is sold under new rules from 16 Nov 2026: the same 8% and 5% targets, 4% daily loss and 8% static max loss, but each phase needs 3 profitable days, each closed with at least 0.5% net profit, where it needed 5 trading days, and the first payout comes 14 days after the first funded trade, where it came after 30. The OLD 2-Step Bright and 2-Step Classic articles (14284817, 14284844) carry the OLD 1-Step's sentence: 'Your rules do not change, except for inactivity: it is now a hard breach and reactivation can be requested until 30 Nov 2026 only.' So does 'BrightFunded Original Accounts (OLD)', for accounts bought before 13 Apr 2026. From 2026-11-17 the 2-Step Bright rows above show the new plan; the 2-Step Classic rows are the OLD plan's.

A new plan, Instant, sold from 16 Nov 2026: no evaluation, funded from the purchase; 3% daily loss; 5% max loss trailing the highest balance or equity and locking at the starting balance; open losses capped at 1% of the starting size; no positions over the weekend (closed at Friday's market close); payouts once five requirements hold together, a 15% consistency rule among them; a split of 90% (100% with a paid add-on). troid does not show it.

_what_troid_compares: What each firm's rules cost the reader at the reader's own sizing: room before the max loss binds, where the ceilings swap, losses survivable, fee drag, liquidation distance. Directory attributes - country, years, reviews, promos - are propfirmmatch's table, not troid's. The two are complementary: they compare firms; troid compares outcomes.
_bitfunded_directory_note: Bitfunded is not listed on propfirmmatch's crypto directory (checked 2026-09-21). It is on troid's compare because troid verified it first, not for a directory rank.
_link_rule: A firm's link appears once troid's operator has confirmed the affiliate terms allow it and the firm's daily limit, max loss, profit target and price each have a recorded source. Until then the link is held. Other cells show 'pending' individually. US availability is always shown as its own row.
_schema_note: Field set borrows from propfirmmatch's per-firm schema (integration/execution type, restricted countries, payment and payout methods, dated rule changes) and adds what they leave empty: the rules themselves, and the computation against the reader's own sizing.
_disclaimer_rule: Generic disclosure text lives in the pages and never names a firm. Anything firm-specific is generated from this file by gen_compare.py: the firms panel on the landing page, and every listed firm's required_disclaimer in the FAQ disclaimer and both footers. Adding or removing a firm is one edit here and one daily run.
_calc_rule: calc is the machine-readable form of the verified rule fields, for troid's desk and ask troid: daily_basis in {initial, day_start, max_balance_equity}, drawdown in {static, trailing}, locks_at_initial_after_pct, hwm_basis in {balance, equity}, fee_per_side_pct, max_leverage. A null is pending and troid's desk says so; it never guesses. Products carry only what their pages state; a product-level key overrides the firm-level one.
_provenance_rule: Every rule field that feeds a number on the site carries provenance: the document, the section, and the date troid read it. Where the repo records no source for a field, the site says 'source not yet recorded' beside it; it never invents one. The evidence for each mapping is in firms_evidence.json.
_availability_rule: availability: the countries each firm's own terms exclude, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. 'excluded' is the firm-wide list, 'platform' lists exclusions that apply to one platform only, 'not_from_terms' records countries a third party lists that troid has not read in the firm's terms (never used to exclude). recorded:false means troid has not extracted the firm's list: the country selector and ask troid say so instead of implying the firm is available. troid never states that a firm is available in a country, only what its record of the firm's terms excludes.
_link_rule_impl: backtest/gen_compare.py link_live(): the entry's link_live is true (set by a human once the affiliate terms exist and their conditions for linking are met) AND compare_product daily_pct, max_pct, target_pct and price each cite a recorded source in provenance.
